SAE regression: an embedding regression decomposed onto SAE directions

Source: R/saereg.R
saereg.Rd

Regresses the document embeddings on a design (OLS, covariates and absorbed fixed effects allowed), takes the coefficient vector of the term of interest, beta, as the effect on the texts, tests it globally, and decomposes it onto the decoder directions W of a sparse autoencoder trained on other texts. Every quantity is linear in the documents: beta = t(E) C, where C, the term's row weights, comes from the design alone (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell).

Usage

saereg(
  formula,
  data,
  W,
  term = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  test = c("permutation", "bootstrap"),
  draws = 999L,
  seed = 7L,
  level = 0.95,
  activations = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

formula

E ~ treat + covariates | fe1 + fe2. The left side is the embedding matrix (documents x dimensions), found in data or in the formula's environment. Fixed effects after | are absorbed (fixest::demean()); combine variables beforehand for interacted effects (e.g. member x stack).

data

Data frame with the variables. Rows with a missing value are dropped.

W

Decoder directions (dimensions x M), unit-length columns, from an SAE trained on texts not used here.

term

Column(s) of the design whose effect is decomposed; default the first variable on the right side. Several terms (e.g. party-specific treatment indicators) are estimated jointly and decomposed one by one.

cluster

One-sided formula, e.g. ~ member: jackknife and bootstrap by cluster. Required with fixed effects or rows.

strata

One-sided formula, constant within clusters: the bootstrap resamples within each stratum (e.g. ever-treated and never-treated members).

test

"permutation" or "bootstrap".

draws

Permutations or bootstrap draws.

seed

Permutations: set.seed(seed) once, then one draw after another. Bootstrap: draw b uses set.seed(seed + b), so any draw can be re-run on its own.

level

Confidence level of the intervals.

activations

Optional SAE activations (documents x M, rows as E).

labels

Optional labels of the M directions.

rows

Optional row of E for each row of data, when rows share an embedding (e.g. a member-day's mean in several stacks); their weights are summed per embedding.

cores

Cores for the jackknife and bootstrap refits (parallel::mclapply).

Value

An object of class saereg: global, features, joint (tibbles), beta (dimensions x terms), weights (C), V_alpha (per term), null (the test's draws of the statistic, draws x terms), and the settings.

Details

Overall effect (global, one row per term):

  • norm_sq_raw = ||beta||^2, biased upward by sampling noise; norm_sq_cor subtracts the noise, sum_k V(beta_k) (Green et al. 2025): the HC2 variance without cluster, the cluster-jackknife variance with it.

  • se, ci_lo, ci_hi: jackknife standard error and normal interval of norm_sq_cor, with the correction held at its full-sample value.

  • p: global test of beta = 0. test = "permutation" (randomized designs, no clusters): Freedman-Lane, the residuals of the model without the term permuted, statistic ||beta||^2. test = "bootstrap" (e.g. difference-in-differences): clusters (or documents) resampled within strata, statistic ||beta_b - beta||^2 against ||beta||^2. Both report p = (1 + #draws >= observed) / (draws + 1).

Decomposition (features, one row per term x direction w_j):

  • alpha = t(w_j) beta: how far the texts move towards (> 0) or away from (< 0) w_j.

  • delta = G^-1 alpha, G = t(W) W: the effect along w_j with the other directions held fixed (beta regressed on all directions).

  • q_j = delta_j alpha_j / ||beta||^2: direction j's share of the effect; the q_j add up to R^2. q_j_cor subtracts the noise, (G^-1 V_alpha)_jj, and divides by norm_sq_cor.

  • Standard errors, intervals and normal p-values from the leave-one-out jackknife: closed form over documents without cluster, refits leaving out one cluster with it.

  • With activations (the SAE's a_ij): gamma, the effect on the activation; on_shift, the effect on 1(a_ij > 0); share_on, the share of documents using j.

Joint shares (joint): R^2 = t(alpha) G^-1 alpha / ||beta||^2, the share of the effect in the span of all directions, raw and corrected; the same for the two and three directions with the largest q_j_cor (biased upward by that selection).
